claims.say: Recall can drop (as more text is in the context).
claims.quote: As token count grows, accuracy and recall degrade, a phenomenon known as context rot.

claims.say: A context window is the amount of text, in tokens, the model can consider at any one time.
claims.quote: The context window (or "context length") of a large language model (LLM) is the amount of text, in tokens, that the model can consider or "remember" at any one time.

claims.say: Think of it as working memory.
claims.quote: An LLM's context window can be thought of as the equivalent of its working memory.

claims.say: The context window works like the model's working memory (not its training data).
claims.quote: This is different from the large corpus of data the language model was trained on, and instead represents a "working memory" for the model.
In real-world terms, the context length of a language model is measured not in words, but in tokens.

claims.say: A decent estimate is roughly 1.5 tokens per word.
claims.quote: But for general purposes, a decent estimate would be roughly 1.5 tokens per word.

claims.say: 1,000 words is about 1,500 tokens (arithmetic on the 1.5 tokens per word estimate; labelled as an example estimate).
claims.quote: There is no fixed word-to-token "exchange rate," ... But for general purposes, a decent estimate would be roughly 1.5 tokens per word.
different models or tokenizers ... might tokenize the same passage of writing differently.

claims.say: When a chat exceeds the window, it must be truncated or summarized.
claims.quote: When a prompt, conversation, document or code base exceeds an artificial intelligence model's context window, it must be truncated or summarized for the model to proceed.

claims.say: The model can consider all of it when the text fits in the window.
claims.quote: The context window ... is the amount of text, in tokens, that the model can consider or "remember" at any one time.
A larger context window allows the model to handle more complex and lengthy prompts, but more context isn't automatically better.

claims.say: As token count grows, accuracy and recall degrade. That's context rot.
claims.quote: As token count grows, accuracy and recall degrade, a phenomenon known as context rot.

claims.say: Double those 1,500 tokens to 3,000, and the model needs 4 times as much processing power (arithmetic on the quoted rule; example numbers).
claims.quote: Compute requirements scale quadratically with the length of a sequence: for instance, if the number of input tokens doubles, the model needs 4 times as much processing power to handle it.

claims.say: Longer input often costs more computing.
claims.quote: increasing context length ... often entails increased computational power requirements—and therefore increased costs

claims.say: Curating what goes in matters as much as the space available.
claims.quote: This makes curating what's in context just as important as how much space is available.

claims.say: Keep only what the answer needs (advice drawn from curating context).
claims.quote: This makes curating what's in context just as important as how much space is available.
